PART XXX1 COMBINED COLD/LOW AIR PRESSURE TESTS

0.
0.1 This

FOREWORD

Indian Standard ( Part XXX1 ) was adopted by the Indian Standards Institution on 19 May 1978, after the draft finalized by the Environmental Testing Procedures Sectional Committee had been approved by the Electronics and Telecommunication Division Council.

0.2 This standard (Part XxX1) deals with combined cold (with gradual change of temperature) and low air pressure tests for both heat dissipating and non-heat dissipating items. 0.2.1 The object of the test is to determine the ability of components or equipment or other articles to be stored and used under a simultaneous combination of low temperature and low air pressure. 0.2.2 This combined test should normally be used only if the effects of combined environments will not be revealed by subjecting the item to single environments. The procedures given in this standard are limited to the case of items which achieve temperature stability during the test procedure. 0.2.3 In the case of testing heat dissipating items, this procedure This test is applicable applies only to the testing of one item at a time. to airborne items and also to those used on ground at high altitudes. At 0.3 The test procedure applies to air pressure down to about 1 kPa. air pressures below 1 kPa, phenomena not taken into account in the design of this test procedure become important. 0.3.1 The relationship between a!titude, pressure and temperature, not been indicated in this standard. standard is based on IEC Publication 68-2-40( 1976 ) `Basic environmental testing procedures, Part 2 : Tests, Test Z/AM : Combined cold/low air pressure tests', issued by the International Electrotechnical Commission. 0.6 This standard should be read in conjunction with the following: procedures procedures for for

0.7 In reporting the result of a test or analysis made in accordance with this standard, if the final value, observed or calculated, is to be rounded off, it shall be done in accordance with IS : 2-1960:.

1. SCOPE 1.1 This standard ( Part XXX1 ) is intended to provide a standard test procedure to determine the suitability of electronic/electrical items for use and/or storage under a combination of low temperature and low air pressure. 1.1.1 This test is primarily
intended for equipment type items.

GENERAL

DESCRIPTION

4.1 This test is a combination

of cold and low air pressure tests. The item is first subjected to the appropriate severity of cold as indicated in the relevant specification. In the case of operational tests, a check is With the then made to ensure that the item is capable of operation. temperature maintained at the indicated value, the chamber air pressure is then reduced to the appropriate severity as specified in the relevant specification. These conditions are maintained for the specified duration.

5.

DESCRIPTION

OF TEST

APPARATUS

Chamber - The chamber shall be capable of maintaining the conditions specified for cold test ( for non-heat dissipating item or for heat for the dissipating item ) and for low air pressure tests. The requirement chamber wall temperature does not apply during periods of temperature or pressure change.
Care shall be taken to avoid air contamination by ancillary equipment and devices and by the air introduced when pressure is restored to normal. 5.2 Mounting - For the testing of heat dissipating item, the mounting yi;$;- test item shall comply with the requirements of IS : 9000 (Part II ): 6.

9.2.8 If required, the operation of the equipment shall be stopped during the temperature/low air pressure conditioning phase, until the internal temperature of the equipment has restabilized so that a subsequent cold switch-on or start-up can be made. 9.2.9 The item shall then be switched off or unloaded.

9.2.10 The chamber pressure shall be restored to normal at a rate not During the increase of pressure, tempeexceeding 10 kFa per minute. NOTE - Measurements preceded by recovery, which would require removal and reintroduction of the items into the chamber, arc not permissible during the conditioning. If it is desired to know the performance of the type of item before the end of the prescribed duration, one additional lot will be required for each specified duration. Recovery and final measurements shall be performed separately for each lot.

11. RECOVERY 11.1 To remove droplets of water, the item mly be shaken by hand or a blast of air at laboratory temperature may be applied for a short duration.
11.2 The item shall then remain under standard recovery conditions for a period adequate for the attainment of temperature stability, with a minimum of one hour. When several items are tested simultaneously and where 1 hour recovery period is inadequate the maximum period for recovery shall be 2 hours and all measurements shall be completed at the end of this period. 11.3 If required by the relevant specification, the item shall be switched on or loaded and measured continuously during the recovery period. 12.
